title: Adversarial model availability scenarios and decision playbook
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Problem: As open and commercial LLM supply becomes more fluid, product and sales teams need a deterministic, repeatable decision process for when a model variant becomes degraded, unavailable, or economically unviable in a target region. This ticket creates an 'adversarial availability' playbook: a catalog of availability failure modes (pricing spikes, quantization regressions, deprecation, region outage, license change), a risk scoring rubric, automated detection signals, and recommended remediations with escalation paths for product, infra, and sales.
objectives: Create a taxonomy of model availability failure modes with example triggers
Define a quantitative risk score combining latency, cost, error-rate, and availability signals
Design alert thresholds and notification flows for Console and PagerDuty/Slack
Produce a step-by-step decision playbook for replacing, throttling, or rolling back a model with minimal customer disruption
Produce a short report for GTM on enterprise contractual risk and suggested mitigations
methodology: Inventory top 25 models by traffic and revenue across regions (use usage analytics + billing exports)
For each model, collect historical time series: token cost, median p95 latency, error-rate, region latency variance, and provisioning failures
Run adversarial scenarios in staging: simulate price spike, simulated KV cache corruption, model binary incompatible downgrade, and regional capacity loss
Interview three enterprise customers and two enterprise AE/CS reps for decision criteria under model outages
Synthesize recommendations and automated thresholds into Console dashboard mocks and an operational runbook
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc published in Confluence with concrete triggers and example incidents
Risk scoring rubric implemented in prototype (not necessarily production) and validated on last 6 months of historical data
Console prototype wireframe showing alerts, per-model risk, and recommended actions reviewed by Reliability PM and Runtime Eng lead
Playbook reviewed and endorsed by Support, Solutions, and Sales leadership
GTM brief (1 pager) and 30-min readout scheduled with Sales Ops
comments: 2026-03-02 - Sofia Alvarez: Kickoff complete. Inventory extraction script assigned to DataOps (ENG-6123). Prioritized starting with models that represent top 80% of token spend.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Chen: Ran initial historical analysis. Observed three large transient cost spikes tied to supplier pricing changes in eu-west-1 during Jan-Feb. Added 'supplier price spike' as primary failure mode.

2026-03-08 - Priya Rao (Reliability PM): Recommended p95 latency delta > 150ms AND error-rate > 0.5% for 10m window to trigger 'degraded' classification. We should test sensitivity on smaller customers.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen: Staging adversarial run complete. KV-cache corruption simulation caused correct fallbacks in 2/3 of cases; need eng work to ensure automatic fallback mapping for quantized variants (ticket ENG-7342 raised).
2026-03-12 - Sales Ops feedback (Jamie Lee): Enterprise contracts require 30-day notice for model discontinuation; playbook must include 'contract-aware remediation' and AE notification template.
2026-03-14 - Sofia Alvarez: Draft playbook uploaded to Confluence. Next: product review with Console PM and Reliability leads on 2026-03-18.
decisions: Use a composite risk score (0-100) combining cost delta, latency delta, error-rate, and capacity error count
Initial alerting to be staged in Slack channel #model-risk-alerts and escalate to on-call only for risk>80
Playbook will prioritize transparent mitigation first: traffic routing to compatible variant, then throttling + quota protection, then customer outreach
Runbook will include AE notification templates and contract clauses inventory for enterprise customers
risks: False positives for transient spikes may cause unnecessary rollbacks—mitigate by requiring 3 consecutive signal windows
Incomplete compatibility mapping between variants could lead to semantic regressions when switching models
Legal/contract obligations may constrain automatic mitigation for some enterprise customers
Telemetry gaps in some regions (APAC edge) may hide early warning signals
deliverables: Console alerting wireframes and notification flows
GTM 1-page brief and AE notification templates
Implementation tickets for ENG and Observability (ENG-7342, ENG-7390)
next_steps: 2026-03-18: Product review with Console PM and Reliability leads
2026-03-20: Run sensitivity analysis on risk thresholds using last 12 months of telemetry
2026-03-25: Customer interview synthesis and inclusion of contract constraints
Create ENG tickets for automatic fallback mapping and observation gaps (ENG-7342, ENG-7390)
Schedule a 30-min GTM readout the week of 2026-04-06

summary_for_execs: Deliver a defensible decision playbook and alerting surface that reduces time-to-remediate when a model variant becomes unreliable or expensive. Outcome: fewer customer-impacting incidents and clearer GTM messaging on fallback and contract implications.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on decision flow and detection thresholds; implementation of automated remediations will be tracked in separate ENG epics.
We will coordinate with Legal on contract-mandated change windows before any automatic model substitution is allowed for enterprise tenants.
